x: Thanks are due to George Clay for his reports which have been appearing in the Wimbledon Borough News. Ernie Duffett continues to do good work in this direction with local papers in the Croydon district.

It is usually the pointsman's lot to arrive back hot and thirsty to find that all the tea and cakes have been gobbled up by the competitors! Amongst regular helpers are Dick Savage, George Clay, Tom Cotton, Charlie Jones, Dave Shepherd and Norman Dewberry and others.
Charlie Cook is recuperating and Will Inge has been ill. George Clay has been troubled by an old malady—an after-effect of being gassed in the 1914-18 war.

Hawkins, a product of George Clay's school, was a good third. Syd Jarlett, although looking a bit thin on top, won the 440 Yards, and Rene Howell, our Poly member, sportingly turned out and gained a point by finishing fifth.

On this day we have as visitors the Leicester Colleges of Art and Technology A.C. and their track secretary is none other than Fred Clay, our old member, and the son of George Clay.

George Clay has received an interesting letter from Frank Craft, our 100 yards champion, who is now resident in Queensland, Australia. He writes to say that he has just failed to qualify for the Olympic selection although he has had a very successful season.
